attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his Substack post, written in his own voice.

semantics.note: The firm "won't" and "will" make this a scorable forecast. It has no deadline. The normalised wording keeps both parts: developers won't get off easily, and copyright lawyers will have plenty of work.

contract.note: The plain reading is continued substantial, contested copyright litigation. That is fair and ordinary. It does not stretch the claim to mean developers must lose. The early-resolution rule fits the forecast's vague, open-ended commitment.

evidence.note: The 12 Aug 2024 Andersen order denied the motions to dismiss the Copyright Act claims against several image-generator developers. This was a ruling on an amended complaint, after an earlier dismissal round. A primary court record, dated after the post.
The Dec 2024 joint filing shows the case moved on to initial disclosures and discovery. This backs up the ongoing legal work.
The same order dismissed the DMCA claims with prejudice. Developers won on some theories, but litigation on the core copyright claims continued.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated, but the early-resolution rule is met. In Aug 2024 a post-publication ruling kept the copyright claims alive against multiple developers after repeated contested proceedings, and discovery followed by Dec 2024. The DMCA dismissal limits how far developers' losses go, but it does not undercut the forecast of a continuing legal burden.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his Substack post.

semantics.note: "Is still on track to be" is a firm statement of expectation about 2024, not a probabilistic hedge, so it is scored. The drafter's modality label "likely" overstates the hedging, but the proposition itself is faithful. The 2023 clause is rhetorical framing.

contract.note: The speaker gave no measure. The plain reading is that GenAI copyright litigation would be a prominent, sustained issue in 2024. That is an ordinary reading of "year of GenAI litigation", and the surrounding copyright discussion supports it. No case count is required, which is fair.

evidence.note: The Aug 2024 Andersen order is a substantive ruling keeping copyright claims alive against Stability, Midjourney, DeviantArt and Runway.
File-stamped complaint showing record labels sued Suno for copyright infringement in June 2024. Infringement is only alleged, but the filing proves the litigation exists.
A separate June 2024 complaint against Udio. This extends the 2024 litigation to music generation.
The DMCA dismissal shows some legal theories failed. That does not contradict the claim that litigation was prominent in 2024.

reviews.rationale: The 2024 horizon has passed. Primary records show substantive copyright rulings against several image-generator developers, and new major-label suits against Suno and Udio, all during 2024. That covers more than one developer and more than one creative sector, which meets the contract's support condition. Some claims failed, but that does not show the disputes were isolated or short-lived.

attribution.note: Marcus is stating his own (joint) argument in his own post and endorses it, adding that nobody disputes it.

semantics.note: A historical observation that some popular image generators had been trained on copyrighted images. Lawfulness is correctly left out of the claim.

contract.note: Fair plain reading. A court admission or court finding about a popular model trained before Jan 2024 settles the claim. Treating Stable Diffusion as popular is reasonable.

evidence.note: The 2025 UK High Court judgment (published before the evaluation date) records Stability's admission that Getty copyright works were used to train v1.4, v2.x and SD XL. All of these were released before the post.
Records that it is agreed all Stable Diffusion versions were trained on LAION-5B subsets. This gives background on the training source but does not by itself show copyright status.
A secondary blog post asserting that training data is mostly copyrighted. It bears on the "nobody disputes" aside, but it is not a primary record of the outcome.

reviews.rationale: In court, Stability admitted that copyright works were used to train several Stable Diffusion versions released before Jan 2024. That meets the support condition. The packet has no contrary evidence. Only one model family is directly covered, but that satisfies "some popular systems".
